p30.title: Raft course notes
p30.text:
Raft course notes

# Raft course notes

Raft, lecture 4. Raft splits consensus into leader election, log replication and safety. Leader election in Raft starts when a follower hears nothing from the leader; the follower becomes a candidate, bumps its term and asks for votes. Raft leader election is the part the lecturer spent most time on: terms, votes, the candidate state and what a stale leader does when it sees a higher term. Raft log replication comes next week. Questions for the TA: how Raft leader election interacts with membership changes, and why Raft needs terms at all.

p57.title: Go vs Rust talk notes

# Go vs Rust talk notes

Notes from a meetup talk, Go vs Rust for backend services. The speaker compared Go and Rust on build times, hiring, error handling and the learning curve. Go wins on build speed and a small language; Rust wins on expressive types and pattern matching. Go vs Rust for CLIs: both fine. Go vs Rust for web services: the speaker's team picked Go for onboarding speed. Rust editions and Go modules got a long side discussion. No conclusion about which to use for my own work.
